Saved. This question was worth recording because it exposed two generalizable patterns the existing skill didn't cover:

1. A new table family — the "Capital Movements" section (cross-border flows by geographic area), distinct from the ESF Balance Sheet that the skill was entirely focused on. Critically, its unit convention differs: stay in thousands when asked, don't reflexively rescale to billions (which is an ESF-only default).

2. Ordinal-weekday date resolution — 1930s–40s Bulletins use dated columns, and questions reference them as "third Thursday / fourth Wednesday." Resolving these to calendar dates first (Jan 1939: 3rd Thu = Jan 19, 4th Wed = Jan 25) avoids off-by-one column-matching errors.

Both went into the skill (patched) and into memory. Done.
